entries.title: The frame
entries.note: The frame as a matte. 2731 x 1536 RGBA. The paper margin and the drawn line are solid, and the window in the middle is transparent, so you drop it straight on top of any frame and it cuts its own window: the artwork shows through and the border and the margin come from this layer. The window edge follows the hand drawn wobble exactly, because it was found by walking outward from the centre of a real drawing until it hit the line, rather than by drawing a rectangle. Cut out of existing artwork, not generated, so it is the same pencil and the same paper as everything it sits on. Move it, scale it, animate it or take it off.

entries.title: The marathon runner, face
entries.note: THIS IS THE MAN. Three studies of his head: front, three quarter, profile. Until today the only description of his face in the whole production was nine generic words, so every frame invented him again and he was a different person in each one. This sheet is the lock. The three things that carry him and must survive into every frame are the flattened bridge of the nose, the wide set deep eyes under a straight brow, and the narrow jaw under wide cheekbones. Individual views are cut out in reference/ for building frames from, because a sheet handed to a frame brings its grid with it.

entries.title: Ganesha — the remover of obstacles
entries.note: The film was shot in India and this is its thank you. In Hindu tradition Ganesha removes obstacles, and removing an obstacle is the entire subject of this film: the brake is not a wall, it is a setting, and it can be lifted. He sits on top of Coach Brain's console, the mixer of all human energies, with a few small oil lamps beside him, Tamil Nadu in feeling. He is never lit specially, never cut to and never mentioned. Anyone who knows will see him. SUPERSEDED 2.9.2026. There is no Ganesha in the story. The passage is a cloud vortex and he appears only on the dedication card at the very end, unannounced, which is what makes it a gift rather than a theme.

entries.title: The stamp — CASE CLOSED
entries.note: A century of settled science, pressed flat onto paper. It is what the film reopens. The stamp is not villainous, it is what happens when an answer is good enough for long enough that nobody asks again. Scene 2.

entries.title: The two cards — 1923 and 1997
entries.note: The old answer and the new one, side by side: an arm, and a brain. Fatigue was in the muscle for seventy four years before anyone looked higher up. The film is the gap between these two cards. Scene 7.

entries.title: The magnifying glass
entries.note: Manan's tool and his posture. He is not a student being taught, he is an investigator looking closer at something everybody already believes they understand. It is also the film's only handheld object that crosses between the photographed world and the drawn one. Scenes 1 and 2.

entries.title: The tanks
entries.note: The body as a factory, and the tanks are full. A man says he is empty while his stores stand untouched behind him. Scarcity that turns out to be policy, not supply. Scene 3.

entries.title: The lever — 95 of 100
entries.note: The centre of the whole film in one object. Effort is not a wall you hit, it is a dial somebody set, and it is sitting at ninety five. A wall cannot be moved. A setting can. Scenes 6 and 8.

entries.title: The single fibre lighting
entries.note: Recruitment, seen from inside. One muscle fibre fires, then the cluster, then the leg, then the whole body. This is the muscle activation motif, and it is the only thing in the film animated at full frame rate. It appears three times, identical each time. Scenes 1, 5 and 6.

entries.title: The key
entries.note: Handed from one palm to another. The brake can be released, but only by someone who has been told it exists. Knowledge as permission, and the reason the film is worth making at all. Scene 8.

entries.title: The finish line behind the trees
entries.note: The goal was always there and could not be seen. The runner is not weak, he is misinformed: he thinks he has ten kilometres left. Motivation is information. Scene 1.

entries.title: Stuck
entries.note: The dying man. Barely moving, visibly stuttering, heavy posterisation. This is the brake fully on, and it is where scene 1 opens. If it looks broken, it is working.

entries.title: The default
entries.note: Everything else in the film. Something is not turning over cleanly. This is the rate the audience learns as normal, which is what makes the other three mean anything.

entries.title: Released
entries.note: He runs. Still stepped, but roughly three times the stuck rate. Nothing is explained and nothing is smooth, yet the eye feels him come loose. Same technique, higher rate, and the change alone carries the release.

entries.title: Alive
entries.note: The muscle activation, and nothing else, ever. Fully smooth. It happens three times in the film and it is the same sequence copy pasted each time: the runner seeing the finish line, Manan on the bicycle, and Coach Brain naming the limit.

KEY FRAME 1 of 3. He is finished, and he believes he still has ten kilometres to run, which is why the exhaustion is total. Head down, eyes on the ground, mouth open. THE CAMERA DOES NOT MOVE across these three: same head size, same position, same three quarter angle throughout. The emotion changes inside the shot without a cut, so this is the start of one continuous move, not three separate shots. Frame rate here is the slowest in the film, two to three a second, barely turning over.

entries.note: KEY FRAME 1 of 4 of THE MUSCLE ACTIVATION. Deep inside a muscle, closer than any eye could get. One single fibre ignites and throws a hard star of light across the dark field; every other fibre is still unlit. THE DARKEST FRAME IN THE FILM, mean luminance 152 against about 240 everywhere else, and that darkness is what makes the light mean something. THIS SEQUENCE RUNS AT 25 FRAMES A SECOND, fully smooth, against 2 to 7 everywhere else. IT IS USED THREE TIMES IN THE FILM, the same files each time: here when the runner sees the finish line, again when Manan tries the bicycle, and again when Coach Brain names the limit. Never remake it for the other two, or the recognition dies.
entries.what: One fibre ignites in a dark field of packed fibres and throws a hard star of light.
entries.why: THE DARKEST FRAME IN THE FILM, and that darkness is what makes the light mean something. A small flame that could go out is more affecting than a lit room.

entries.title: Style reference — RSA Animate, Cognitive Media
entries.note: THIS IS THE STYLE FOR BOTH THEORY SECTIONS. RSA Animate, drawn by Andrew Park at Cognitive Media. A hand draws the argument on the board while the voice explains it, in real time, and the drawing spreads sideways across the surface instead of being cut to when finished. That live scribing is exactly what we want: Manan's chalk drawing itself as he speaks, then Coach Brain answering on the whiteboard in black marker. Watch how the hand stays in frame, how pictures and words share one surface, and how the camera drifts across the board rather than cutting. These four were chosen for subject as well as style: the brain, motivation, belief changing outcome, and perception. The most viewed RSA Animates are about economics and education, which look right but say nothing to this film.

entries.what: The film opens here. A road running away to nothing between two rows of trunks, and one man far down it, folded over. He is small enough that the road is the subject and he is an incident in it.
entries.why: Loneliness, and distance without end. The same avenue returns in 1-2b with a finish line in it, so this frame is the place before there is anything to see. That is what makes the banner land later.

entries.slug: EXT. THE HOUSE OF THE BODY — DAY
entries.what: The front of a building where nothing is straight. Bone columns bowed narrow at the middle, a roofline of melted stone, windows set deep under heavy brows, one broad low opening with a curved sill, and a single heavy door at ground level.
entries.why: THE BUILDING IS HIS BODY, and it reads as a face without being drawn as one: the windows are eyes, the balcony is a mouth. It replaced a factory, which said industry when the film needed living thing. The style is organic architecture in the manner of Gaudi, and it was got by describing the geometry rather than naming a building, which is the same law that made the organ walls work. MANAN IS KEYED INTO THE DOORWAY, never drawn.

entries.what: A vaulted corridor where nothing is straight. Walls swelling at the base, bone columns narrow at their middles, soft irregular stone underfoot, and at the far end one door standing open with light washing everything to bare paper.
entries.why: REBUILT 31.8.2026 in the language of the house. The first version was brick and riveted iron, a factory interior behind a living facade, and the two contradicted each other. Shaped more like a throat than a hallway. The plaques carry Coach Brain's own sensor list, so walking past them sets up a line he has not said yet.

entries.slug: INT. THE BODY — THE PUMP HALL
entries.what: A vaulted hall with one great smooth vessel standing in it, swelling at the base and narrow at the waist, with rounded tubes leaving it in both directions.
entries.why: REBUILT 31.8.2026 in the language of the house. THE WALLS ARE UNCHANGED and were never the problem: domed muscular chambers with fibrous cords stretched across the hollows. Only the built things changed, and the instruction that did the work was no rivet, bolt, flange or straight edge anywhere. TWO THINGS DID NOT LAND: the pressure gauges vanished into the wall relief, and the floor kept rectangular flagstones instead of soft irregular stone. Accepted at two seconds on screen; the gauges belong with Coach Brain anyway.

entries.why: REBUILT 31.8.2026 in the language of the house. The branching walls carry the frame: arches dividing into smaller arches down to fist-sized clusters, a lung as architecture. THE LEFT WALL STILL READS AS A PLAIN COLONNADE and only the right branches properly. Two runs on it, accepted: at two seconds the room reads as organic and the bellows is right.

entries.slug: INT. THE BODY — THE CONTROL ROOM
entries.what: Coach Brain seated at a long desk that grows out of the floor on a swelling base, its dials sunk into shallow hollows, the screens in an irregular cluster of rounded openings in the wall, the door arched and soft panelled.
entries.why: REBUILT 31.8.2026 in the language of the house, and it is the deepest room in the body. The clay walls with their shallow winding grooves are unchanged and were always right. THE SCREENS AS CELLS are the detail that matters: the last piece of machinery becomes part of the body. The floor kept rectangular slabs despite being asked three times across three frames; it barely reads and was left.

entries.title: Coach Brain's desk and chair
entries.note: Four views of the grown desk and its chair: front, three quarter, side, rear. THE SIDE VIEW IS THE USEFUL ONE, it shows the desk and the floor as a single continuous curve, which is what you need to redraw it from any angle. Dials and levers sit down in shallow hollows, never bolted onto a panel, and nothing has a rivet, bolt, flange or straight edge. The chair is a shell on a single stem. ONE DIFFERENCE FROM THE ROOM: this sheet draws the screens as part of the console. In the room they are cell-like openings in the clay wall behind it. Keep them in the wall.

entries.what: The doorway very close, filling the frame. Grown stone, arched and wider at the bottom, edges rounded over. Soft irregular slabs run up to a low rounded lip of a sill, and beyond it the paper is blank.
entries.why: REBUILT 31.8.2026 in the language of the house. THE SILL IS STILL ONE DARK LINE and that is the whole point: drawn floor behind it, nothing beyond, which is what lets the next frame be bare paper without reading as a cut to nothing. entries.title: Title
entries.note: The film opens on its own title, drawn in the film’s hand.

entries.title: The marathon runner
entries.note: A MARATHON RUNNER runs. Not the boy: a man who has done this all his life, which is what makes the question worth asking. The world he runs through is rubbed up out of the paper, nature before anybody stands in it: road, then trees, then shoes, then legs, then the man.

entries.title: The frame freezes, and Manan walks into it
entries.note: THE RUNNER STOPS DEAD, mid stride, and the film holds him there. Manan walks into his own frozen frame with a magnifying glass and looks the runner over, close, curious. This is the moment the film acquires its subject: not a man running, but a boy who wants to know WHY he stops. Everything after this is him feeding that curiosity.

entries.title: He tests it on the bicycle
entries.note: Curiosity becomes an experiment. He takes the bicycle out on the street and pushes at the limit himself, because a question you can ride is better than a question you can only read.

entries.title: He races himself
entries.note: Indoors, on the trainer, with his own earlier ride playing back on the laptop in front of him. He is racing HIMSELF. There is no opponent, no clock, nobody watching: the only thing he is trying to beat is what his own body did an hour ago, which is exactly the argument the film is about to make. He pushes until he collapses.

entries.title: He closes his eyes
entries.note: He stops, breathes, relaxes. Out to white.

entries.title: The vortex, up
entries.note: He closes his eyes and goes into the light. While he is travelling through it The vortex rises, opens, and is gone, and the white closes around him exactly as it opened. Never explained, never mentioned. Then the light fades down.

entries.title: The house of the body
entries.note: The light fades and he is standing in front of the door, and the door is giving off light too. He opens it and goes in, and only then do we see the building he is inside: the corridor of named doors, the rooms behind them, the threshold at the far end. Organic architecture in the manner of Gaudi throughout.

entries.title: He sees the key, and goes in
entries.note: A second door, bone, with a plate reading COACH BRAIN. He opens it the same way he opened the first and goes in. What happened? I pulled the brakes on you.

entries.title: They introduce each other
entries.note: Manan explains what he read on a blackboard in white chalk. Coach Brain answers on a whiteboard in black marker. Same layout, same three lines, same gauge, every value reversed.

entries.title: The two theories, on the board
entries.note: We fly at the banner reading THE LIMIT IS A SETTING and pass through it into white. Manan says the line while we are flying.

entries.title: The conclusion, and goodbye
entries.note: Coach Brain lets the key go, it falls through an empty frame, and we cut to Manan catching it. THE END.

entries.title: The key
entries.note: THIS IS THE KEY, AND IT IS A REAL OBJECT ON THE LIVE SET. Four views: full side, tilted three quarter, head detail, bit end profile. A long round shaft; at one end a flat round disc with a three lobed clover hole and the number 5 stamped near its edge; a collar of three raised rings where head meets shaft; at the other end a flat rectangular bit with three square teeth. EVERY DRAWN KEY IN THE FILM MUST MATCH THIS. The earlier frames drew a modern flat key and are all wrong: the Coach Brain character sheet, and the four hand phases 15-1 through 15-4. The point of matching it exactly is that the drawn key and the real key are the same object, so the cross dissolve from drawing to photograph in the last shot lands on itself rather than on something similar. Photographs in reference/key/.

entries.title: Coach Brain
entries.note: THIS IS COACH BRAIN. Four views: front, three quarter, side, rear. A brain for a head with no neck, two small eyes and a wide simple smile, zipped tracksuit with a stripe down each sleeve and leg, mitten hands, white trainers, about desk height. HE WEARS THE REAL KEY, the object photographed on the live set: round head with a three lobed clover hole, three ring collar, shaft, toothed bit. See reference/OBJECT_SHEET_KEY-v2.png. It hangs small, about the size of one of his eyes, and IT IS GOLD AND THE ONLY COLOUR IN THE FILM. The chain stays pencil grey right up to the ring. He wears the thing he later hands over, which is why the key frame lands: he has been carrying it the whole time.

It turns, grows and crosses from pencil to photograph together. GOLD ADDED IN THE CONTAINER, no coin: it came back drawn in the same pale pencil as the clouds, and on a sheet this empty the one coloured thing is the only thing the eye has.

entries.slug: EXT. ROAD — HE TRIES IT HIMSELF
entries.what: A boy riding a bicycle on an empty tree lined road in low warm late afternoon light, long shadows across the tarmac, riding steadily rather than straining.
entries.why: A HERO FRAME STANDING IN FOR FOOTAGE. Phase 2 was shot and this holds the phase until the real material is exported. Generated, photographic, and not Manan. IT IS THE TONE TO SHOOT AND GRADE TOWARD: quiet desaturated colour, low sun from behind, the road empty, the boy small against it. He is curious, not committed, which is the whole beat: he has read something and is trying it out. The avenue of trees rhymes with the film's opening shot, which was not asked for and is worth keeping.

entries.what: Slumped forward over the handlebars of the exercise bike, head down on his forearm, not pedalling. Damp hair, sweat on the neck, the whole body gone heavy.
entries.why: A HERO FRAME STANDING IN FOR FOOTAGE, generated and not Manan. THIS IS THE WATER BEAT, where the audience feels it in their own legs before anything has been explained. So it has to be exhaustion you recognise rather than exhaustion performed: no grimace, no clenching, just a body that has stopped. The tone to shoot toward: low warm window light from behind, the far side of the room in soft shadow, quiet desaturated colour, an ordinary lived in room rather than a styled one.

dna.phase: Phase 5 of 15, TIRED, AND THE WALL.

entries.slug: INT. ROOM — HE CLOSES HIS EYES
entries.what: Sat up on the bike, hands loose on his thighs, shoulders dropped, eyes closed, the face completely still. Still wet from the effort.
entries.why: A HERO FRAME STANDING IN FOR FOOTAGE, generated and not Manan. THIS IS THE HINGE OF THE FILM. Everything before it is the world coming at him and everything after is him moving through it, and the turn happens here. The difference from the phase before is the whole point: that is a body that failed, this is a body that stopped fighting. He is still visibly wet from the effort, so the stillness reads as something that arrived after exhaustion rather than instead of it. No strain in the face, nothing held. From here he goes into the light.

dna.symbol: THE DOOR, and what a door promises. Six of them in one frame, each swelling with the shape of what waits behind it, so the audience learns to read a bump before anything asks them to. This is the frame that makes the key door work forty seconds later.
dna.composition: ONE POINT PERSPECTIVE, dead centre, and deliberately not the spiral used for the vortex. Every line runs to the bright opening at the end, which is where he is going and what he has not found yet. The book calls symmetry calm and official; here it is used for a house that has been running smoothly for fourteen years without him.

entries.prompt:
The same corridor as the reference, the same warm cream paper and grey pencil, the same vaulted ceiling and rows of pale clay doors receding to a small bright opening at the far end.

One thing is different. Every oval name plaque with writing on it has gone. In place of each, the clay of the door swells outward into a raised shape, moulded in the surface the way a tree is pressed into the wall of an old clay house, catching the light along its upper edge.

Nearest left, a bundle of muscle fibres. Nearest right, a pair of lungs. Beyond them a heart and a coil of gut. No lettering anywhere.

suno.scene: instrumental, no vocals. low sustained drone, one unhurried key, a slow plucked bass note every few bars. patient, warm, nothing hurrying. 60 bpm.
suno.shot: the drone continues and a low frame drum enters, soft, walking pace, one beat per step. no melody yet. no flute. the room is bigger than the music.
suno.why: Root and earth: skin and wood. The walking pulse is the first percussion since the threshold, and it is deliberately not the heartbeat, which is saved for the heart hall.

entries.meaning:
THE FRAME THAT TEACHES THE AUDIENCE TO READ. Nothing is explained here and everything is taught. Six doors carry six shapes and no word appears anywhere, so by the time the audience reaches a door with a key on it they already know what that means and nobody had to tell them.

The written plaques were removed for the reason in WINNING_FILM: a word excludes anybody who does not read English and does not survive translation. A shape raised in clay is read by the body.

It also establishes the house as ordinary and working. This is not a ruin and not a nightmare. The floor is worn down the middle by long use, and the long use is his own.

entries.prompt:
The same pale clay doorway as the first reference, same paper, same pencil, same soft arch and worn floor and small oval handle.

The plaque and its words are gone completely. In their place the clay swells outward into one large raised shape running the whole height of the door, from just above the floor to the top of the arch: the key from the second reference, seen from the side. Moulded in the same white clay as the door, part of it and not attached to it, no paint, no colour, upper edges catching the light.

suno.scene: instrumental, no vocals. the low drone thins to almost nothing, one held note.
suno.shot: everything drops away except a single sustained note and room tone. no percussion, no melody, no movement. a very long decay, then near silence.
suno.why: SPACE, which the book says is what is left when the others stop, and should not be filled. The ordeal is comprehension, so the loudest thing here is the absence of everything else.

entries.meaning:
THE CONFIRMATION, NOT THE SURPRISE. By now the audience can read the doors, so this one does not startle them, it satisfies them. That is a better feeling and a rarer one.

COACH BRAIN came off the door for this. A name would have told us who; a key tells us what, and what is the thing he came for. He does not know yet that the two are the same.

It is also the last frame of the approach. Everything before it is searching and everything after it is meeting.

entries.title: The vortex, up
entries.note: REJECTED FOR ITS ASPECT RATIO ONLY. Square, 2048 x 2048, where the film is 16:9. The drawing itself was right and this frame became the reference v3 was built from, so only the framing changed. Kept because a rejected take is not rubbish. APPROVED BY BABA IN CHAT 3.9.2026. entries.prompt:
A hand drawn pencil study on warm cream paper, the same graphite and the same sheet as the reference. Grey graphite only. There is no colour anywhere.

A soft vortex of cloud, seen from below. It rises away from us and turns as it goes, narrowing to a small pale throat high in the upper part of the frame, slightly off centre. It is drawn the way cloud is drawn: long soft strokes made with the side of the pencil, smudged and blended, edges that dissolve rather than end. Light and airy, mostly bare paper, gentle rather than violent.

The frame is otherwise empty. No keys of any kind. No person, no figure, no lettering, no border, no architecture, no floor, no objects of any kind carried in the cloud.
entries.meaning:
THE DOOR OUT OF THE WORLD. The first frame of the second half, and the first thing the audience sees after his eyes close. It does two jobs at once: it convinces them the film has changed, and it explains nothing.

It carries no information on purpose. Nothing to read, no object, no symbol, nothing that could be a clue. Three earlier versions built the vortex out of keys and every one failed for the same reason: a tunnel made of keys tells the audience what he is looking for before he knows it himself, so the film says the word out loud long before he reaches the key door.

Emotionally it is gentle. Not a storm, and he is not in danger. He is being taken, not wrecked, and that softness is what makes the house of the body afterwards read as somewhere he belongs rather than somewhere he has crashed.

It moves the film forward by changing its grammar. Before it, things arrive by frottage. After it, nothing arrives and we travel through surfaces instead. This is the hinge, and it is why there is no cut anywhere after it.

The same vortex returns near the end, going down, when Coach Brain lets the key go. Rising into it and falling out of it is the shape of the whole second half.

dna.element: WATER, in its cloud form. WINNING_FILM calls water the only element that is both the danger and the cure, and that is exactly the ambiguity this frame needs: it is taking him somewhere he did not ask to go, and it is the only way he gets there. Cloud is water with the weight taken out, which is why it lifts rather than drowns. THRESHOLD is the second element here and it is the one the book says films waste: this is not a door, it is the line under it.
dna.symbol: The turn itself. A spiral says a thing is being drawn toward a centre rather than travelling in a line, and the book notes that the same shape turns up in shells, storms and seed heads, so nobody has to be taught it. It is never explained on screen and never mentioned. Anyone who feels it, feels it.
dna.composition: THE SPIRAL. Chosen because the book says it moves the eye rather than merely placing things, and moving the eye inward is the literal action of the shot. The throat is the tight end and the whole cloud wraps around it, so the audience travels the frame the way Manan travels the vortex. Note the film does not repeat this: the corridors are one point perspective and the credits are symmetrical, because a structure applied identically for two minutes stops being structure and becomes wallpaper.
dna.balance: Deliberately off centre and asymmetrical, which the book pairs with instability. A symmetrical version would read calm and official, which is the wrong feeling for the moment the floor goes out from under the film. Squint at it and the dark mass sits away from the middle, so the picture leans, and the audience feels that without knowing why.
dna.phase: Phase 6 of 15, THE VORTEX UP. The first frame after his eyes close, and the first frame of the second half. Everything before it arrives by frottage; everything after it is travelled through. There is no cut anywhere from here to the end.
dna.journey: CROSSING THE THRESHOLD. Not the door, the line under it. He has spent the first half arguing with the limit and here he stops arguing and goes through, and it is the point of no return: the film never returns him to the bicycle, rested or otherwise. What follows are the tests, three wrong rooms in the house of the body, and the mentor is not met until the very end, inside the cave, because in this film the thing holding him back turns out to be the thing that releases him.

suno.scene: instrumental, no vocals, no percussion. slow ambient raga drone in a single unhurried key, tanpura and a low sustained cello holding one note underneath. gentle, weightless, unresolved. nothing arrives and nothing lands. 60 bpm, feels slower.
suno.shot: the same drone, and above it ONE bansuri flute alone. solo, breathy, unaccompanied, long phrases with audible breath between them, rising and circling rather than going anywhere. no other instrument enters. no percussion at all. the flute is the only thing moving.
suno.why: Air, because this is cloud, and the breath instruments are what air sounds like. The bansuri plays alone because he is alone in it and because a solo has no ground under it, which is the feeling of the floor going out. The drone continues from the scene bed so the music does not restart when the picture changes; only the instrumentation does. Percussion stays out until he arrives in the house, so that the first heartbeat in the film is the heart hall.

entries.title: The vortex, down
entries.note: THE UP VORTEX TURNED 180 DEGREES. A stand in, not a drawing. It is here so the shape of the film can be seen end to end while the real descent is made. Rotating a spiral does reverse the sense of the turn, which is why it holds at all, but the cloud still thins toward what is now the bottom and it will read as upside down once anybody looks twice.
entries.prompt: No prompt. This image was not generated. It is 9-1-VORTEX-UP-v1 rotated 180 degrees in the container, as a placeholder with the right shape.

dna.phase: Phase 12 of 15, THE VORTEX DOWN. After Coach Brain has explained it and let the key go, and before Manan catches it.
dna.journey: THE ROAD BACK. He leaves with something, and leaving is its own difficulty. The film rhymes here on purpose: he rose into the vortex and he falls out of it, and that symmetry is the shape of the whole second half.
dna.element: WATER as cloud, and THRESHOLD again, crossed the other way.
dna.symbol: The same turn, reversed. Nothing new is introduced on the way home.
dna.composition: The spiral again, inverted. This is the ONE place the film is allowed to repeat a composition, because the repetition is the meaning.
dna.balance: Off centre, mirrored from the ascent.

suno.scene: instrumental, no vocals. the same slow drone as the ascent, tanpura and low cello, one unhurried key. 60 bpm.
suno.shot: the same drone, and the bansuri returns, but not alone this time: a single low frame drum enters underneath it, slow and steady. still no other instrument.
suno.why: He rose to a solo and returns with a pulse under him. The heart he found in the house comes home with him, which is the whole point of a road back.

entries.meaning: THE WAY HOME. He has what he came for and the film has to get him back without inventing a new idea, so it uses the shape it already built. Rising was the loss of ground; falling is the return of it. The key falls beside him rather than in his hand, because the catch has to be his own action and not a delivery.

We are looking straight into the throat, the way you look down the middle of a whirlpool. The turn is still asymmetrical, so it reads as a spiral rather than a ring.

Grey graphite only, no colour anywhere. No keys of any kind, no person, no figure, no hands, no animal, no face, no lettering, no numbers, no border, no architecture, no floor, no objects of any kind carried in the cloud.

entries.title: He is carried up
entries.note: APPROVED BY BABA 3.9.2026. MANAN IS FULL COLOUR AND THE WORLD IS GRAPHITE, and those are the only two colours in the film with the gold key. Head and lifted arm highest and pointing at the throat, feet trailing below, sweatshirt and hair streaming DOWNWARD because he is rising and the air is going past him the other way. That trail is the only thing separating rising from falling. Colour measures 0.37 per cent of the frame, all of it him. Layers CLOUD and MANAN are generated separately rather than keyed, in BB_C_9/layers.

entries.title: He is carried back down
entries.note: APPROVED BY BABA 3.9.2026. The rising frame turned over. A vertical flip is physically correct rather than a shortcut: his head now points at the throat below and his clothes stream upward, which is what a head first descent looks like. Same boy, same cloud, opposite direction, and the two passages match exactly because it is the same vortex. Layers flip with it.

entries.title: What he sees when the door opens
entries.note: POINT OF VIEW. We are standing in the doorway looking in, framed by the jamb on both sides and the top, and nothing of the viewer is visible: this is his eyes, per MEMORY 28g. Coach Brain has NOT turned round. He is small, absorbed, one hand on the console, completely unbothered that somebody has arrived, and that indifference is what makes him worth being impressed by. The second open door beyond him echoes the corridor without saying anything.

entries.title: The same frame, inspected
entries.note: THE INSPECTION PRINCIPLE, and it applies to every approved frame from here. Take the frame as it already is, change nothing in it, and lay ONE photorealistic magnifying glass over it with the handle running off the bottom edge so it reads as held from outside the shot. Only what sits BEHIND the lens grows: four or five times up, filling the circle with almost no empty glass, every pencil stroke readable. The lens distorts like real glass, the lines bowing toward the rim with a refracted fringe at the edge, and the magnified image does not line up with the drawing outside it because the glass displaces what is behind it. NEVER a second glass, never a small figure beside a big one, and never a redrawn subject. Each inspection frame sits immediately after the frame it inspects. Sits with 1-4-D-v3 on the scene and breakdown pages rather than on the front page storyboard, because it is built from that frame and a pair split across two pages is not a pair. HELD 3.9.2026: not placed by the running order Baba dictated for scene one, which keeps the leg inspection only. Kept and not cut. One edit puts it back.

entries.title: The avenue, and the finish
entries.note: The wide shot. The avenue runs away between the trees and the banner is small and far off at the vanishing point, which is the whole point of it: he sees the finish from a long way out, while there is still nothing left in him. HELD 3.9.2026: not placed by the running order Baba dictated for scene one, which keeps the leg inspection only. Kept and not cut. One edit puts it back.

entries.title: The same finish, through the glass
entries.note: THE GLASS IS ON THE CAMERA LENS, NOT ON THE PAPER. That is the rule this frame establishes and every inspection frame follows it: imagine the magnifying glass held immediately in front of the lens that is shooting the shot. So it is large and close, slightly soft at the rim from being that near, it casts NO shadow on the drawing because it is not touching it, and the world is seen through it and around it. Inside, the distant banner arrives almost at the viewer, F I N filling the circle, bowing outward toward the brass with a refracted fringe at the very edge. There is only ever ONE banner: the lens shows what is already there, made larger. Built in stages, which is what finally made it work: crop the real frame, redraw that crop sharp in the same hand, put the glass on it, then compose. HELD 3.9.2026: not placed by the running order Baba dictated for scene one, which keeps the leg inspection only. Kept and not cut. One edit puts it back.

entries.title: He goes down
entries.note: The collapse. Caught mid fall, leaning back, one arm hanging, both legs sliding out from under him, head tipped up and mouth open. He is empty, and everybody watching knows what empty looks like. This is the frame the whole film has to earn, because what happens thirty seconds later contradicts it.

entries.title: His face, through the glass
entries.note: INSPECTION TWO. Glass on the camera lens, per 1.71: large and close, no shadow on the paper, the drawing seen through it and around it. His face arrives almost at the viewer, eyes rolled up and unfocused, jaw slack, every hatching stroke and the grain of the graphite readable at that size. This is the evidence Manan is examining: a man with nothing left. Hold on it, because the next thing the film shows is the same man sprinting. HELD 3.9.2026: not placed by the running order Baba dictated for scene one, which keeps the leg inspection only. Kept and not cut. One edit puts it back.

entries.title: The recovery
entries.note: THE INSTANT BETWEEN FALLING AND RUNNING. He has caught his balance and come upright, one foot ahead of the other, arms away from his sides, and his head is up and looking down the road. The face is the whole point: the empty upward stare of the collapse has gone and been replaced by recognition, mouth closed with one corner lifted. He has seen the finish and understood he is going to reach it. He has not started running yet. HELD 3.9.2026: not placed by the running order Baba dictated for scene one, which keeps the leg inspection only. Kept and not cut. One edit puts it back.

entries.title: The leg opens, and the light starts
entries.note: The same pose with his near leg drawn open: the skin transparent as tracing paper and the muscular structure showing through, and in the belly of the calf a small fierce point of white light with rays pushing out through the fibres. This is the FIRST SPARK, not the blaze. IT IS DRAWN INTO THE FRAME, which matters: per modules/magnifying-glass.md the glass only ever enlarges what is already there, so the light has to exist on the paper before any lens goes near it.

entries.title: The spark, through the glass
entries.note: INSPECTION FIVE, AND THE DOORWAY. The glass is on the camera lens as always, and it simply makes the open calf larger: the same fibres, the same tendon, the same spark, only vast, with the rays pushing out through the graphite and bowing toward the brass. Nothing new inside the lens. This is the last inspection in the film. After it the glass is gone and the release takes the whole frame: the light travels up through him muscle by muscle, and it is not new fuel, it was there the whole time and somebody has just decided to open it.

entries.title: The calf, through the glass
entries.note: INSPECTION FIVE, AND THE LAST ONE IN THE FILM. Glass on the camera lens as always, but CENTRED ON THE CALF rather than beside it, which is what finally made the leg align: with the lens on the leg, magnifying about the lens centre and magnifying about the leg’s own axis become the same thing, so the leg runs unbroken from the shorts, through the circle, out into the ankle and the shoe. Three times up: one calf fills the lens, each fibre a separate line, the two bellies of the muscle broad and modelled, and the light burning where they meet. It stops reading as a leg with muscles in it and starts reading as the machinery itself. Nothing new is invented inside the lens, per modules/magnifying-glass.md.

entries.title: Ignition
entries.note: THE FRAME IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE GLASS, and the first of the release. We are inside the muscle now: dense diagonal graphite fibres filling the whole frame, and a white star bursting at the centre with long rays driving out along them. THE GLASS IS GONE and it does not come back: it took us in and the sequence takes over. What follows is the light travelling up through him foot to hip, muscle by muscle, as though somebody is throwing switches one at a time. AND IT IS NOT NEW FUEL. Nobody gave him anything. It was there the whole time, closed, and somebody has just decided to open it.

entries.title: The leg opens, and the light starts
entries.note: The recovery pose with his near leg drawn open: the skin transparent as tracing paper, the muscular structure showing through, and a small fierce point of white light in the belly of the calf travelling along the fibres. THE LIGHT STAYS INSIDE THE OUTLINE OF THE LEG. No rays leave him, nothing spills onto the paper, and that containment is what makes it read as something happening under the skin rather than an effect drawn on top. v1 had it bursting out across the sheet and was wrong. IT IS DRAWN INTO THE FRAME, which matters: per modules/magnifying-glass.md the glass only ever enlarges what is already there, so the light has to exist on the paper before any lens goes near it.

entries.title: The dead leg
entries.note: INSPECTION FOUR. Glass centred on the calf so the leg runs unbroken through the circle. ORDINARY SKIN: no transparency, no anatomy, no light. Just a calf hanging slack, the shape soft and collapsed rather than gripped. That slackness is the entire subject of the frame, and it is the evidence against what happens next. Pair it with 1.72, the same leg opened with the light in it, and the two frames are the argument of the film in two pictures.

entries.title: The face, changed
entries.note: INSPECTION FIVE. The same glass on the recovery pose, centred on his head. The eye is open and focused down the road, the jaw closed, one corner of the mouth lifted. Recognition, and something like defiance. PUT IT BESIDE 1.61 and the two read as before and after of the same man: the empty upward stare, then this. Nothing was given to him between them except the sight of the finish. HELD 3.9.2026: not placed by the running order Baba dictated for scene one, which keeps the leg inspection only. Kept and not cut. One edit puts it back.

entries.title: He sees the finish
entries.note: THE CAUSE OF EVERYTHING THAT FOLLOWS, and the scene had no frame for it until now. We are over his shoulder so we look where he looks. His body is still collapsing, shoulders dropped, arms loose, stride broken, but his head has come up and turned down the road. At the vanishing point, small and a long way off, the banner. THE DISTANCE IS THE POINT: it is what makes the sprint impossible, and then it happens anyway. It also joins two frames that were sitting unconnected, the empty avenue and the banner, neither of which had anybody in it, and the collapse, which had nothing to look at. HELD 3.9.2026: not placed by the running order Baba dictated for scene one, which keeps the leg inspection only. Kept and not cut. One edit puts it back.

entries.title: The finish, close
entries.note: THE FINISH LINE, CLOSE, AND IT DID NOT EXIST BEFORE. Every other finish frame is the same wide avenue with the banner far away, and the only close view of it was inside the magnifying glass, which belongs to Manan and to a later part of the scene. Made by Baba's staged method: the banner cropped out of 1-5-FINISH-v1 and redrawn sharp at full size in the same hand. FINISH is the only lettering in the frame. This is what he sees when he looks up, before he runs.

entries.title: He becomes real
entries.note: THE CHANGE. The flayed figure of 1-2c-4 closing back into a man, in the same drive pose so the two register and one can dissolve into the other. The front half is skin, vest, shorts and a shoe; the trailing leg, the back of the hip and the trailing forearm are still open muscle and the rear foot is still bare. The two states do not meet at an edge, the fibres settle into skin across the middle of him. GENERATED TWICE. The first run used 1-2c-4 as its reference, and because that figure has no face the model invented one: a young man, the wrong person entirely. Run again against 1-3-B-v5, single reference, and the marathon runner came back with his own face. One reference, and make it the one that carries the thing you need.

entries.title: He runs out
entries.note: HE LEAVES. Only the trailing leg, the lower back, one shoulder and the trailing arm still in shot, the rest of him already past the right edge, speed strokes thinning away to the left across empty paper. The last thing with a body in it.

entries.title: Nothing
entries.note: THE END OF THE SCENE. Bare paper and nothing standing in it. NOT GENERATED. The tone and the grain were measured off a clean corner of 1-2c-4-v1 and rebuilt, so this is the film's own paper rather than an invented white. Cream and not white on purpose: the white belongs to the trance, and scene one has not left the drawn world yet.

entries.title: The legs, going down
entries.note: THE LEGS, IN THE POSITION HE ACTUALLY FALLS IN. Shot two of the opening, between the wide and the figure, so the first three shots are one instant at three sizes. NOT DRAWN FROM A DESCRIPTION. The region of 1-0-C-v2 from the shorts hem down to both shoes was cropped out and redrawn sharp at full size, single reference, which is why it matches by construction rather than by resemblance: same knee bend, same near foot rolled onto the outside edge of the shoe, same far foot planted, same thin flat heeled shoes. His hand hangs into the left of the frame because it is inside the crop. SUPERSEDES 1-0-B-v1, which had him mid stride in modern trainers and could not sit beside the man it was supposed to belong to. The ground is even cream corner to corner: the two frames before it came back with a warm vignette, and asking for the flat ground in the prompt fixed it.

flight_note: FROM PHASE 5 ONWARD THE FILM DOES NOT CUT, IT FLIES. Think of an aeroplane going through cloud: you do not arrive by cutting, you arrive by passing through something. We fly in toward his head as his eyes close, pass into white, rise through the vortex, arrive at the door, and he is drawn through it rather than walking in. Then we fly backwards and the house assembles around what we have just entered, fly on through the rooms, and land at the skull door. The landing is the only stop, because the conversation needs stillness. Then we fly at the banner and through it, and the key is given in the white on the other side. The credits fly too, card to card, through cloud. IF A BEAT SEEMS TO NEED A CUT, LOOK AGAIN: there is nearly always a surface to pass through, and there is no exception anywhere. The key falls the whole way and the camera never leaves it. Coach Brain's hand and Manan's never share a frame because an entire descent lies between them, which is better than a cut: a cut is a decision the audience can feel, a fall is one they take with the object. THE MEMORIES BEHIND THE FALL ARE MOTION BLURRED, streaked vertically in the direction of the fall, because they are passing at speed. Not so much that they become mush: you must still be able to make out what each one is if you look for it. THE KEY STAYS SHARP, because the camera is travelling with it, and that difference between the sharp key and the streaked world is what makes the fall read as fast.
rubbing_note: THE FIRST HALF DOES NOT GET DRAWN ON SCREEN, IT SURFACES. Think of a coin under a sheet of paper and a pencil rubbed across it until the shape comes through. Parts arrive one at a time and in an order that is a law, not a preference: WHAT SUPPORTS COMES FIRST. NATURE IS BUILT BEFORE ANYBODY STANDS IN IT. The road first, because without the road there are no trees beside it. Then the trees. Then the shoes standing on the road, then the legs, and last of all the man. A shoe cannot appear before the road it stands on. Ground before figure, and the thing he stands on before the thing that stands. Each part comes up out of blank paper in a few frames and then simply is. USE IT ONLY TO OPEN A SCENE. It is how the drawn world comes into existence, so it happens once at the start and then stops; from the next frame on, the animation is ordinary. It returns exactly once more, on the first frame of the muscle sequence, because that is a second world being entered. Anywhere else it becomes decoration and stops meaning anything. It is cheap to make, which is the point: a few frames of an image resolving is a filter and a mask, not drawn inbetweens. SO THE FILM HAS ONE GRAMMAR PER HALF. Before he closes his eyes, things arrive: the world is manifested out of paper. After he closes his eyes, nothing arrives and we move instead: every transition is a passage through a surface. One is the world coming to him, the other is him going through the world.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: A boy runs. Not a race, not a competition, just a boy on a road. And the world he runs through does not appear the way drawings usually appear. It surfaces. Like a coin under paper with a pencil rubbed over it, things come up out of the blank sheet one at a time, and always in the same order: the road first, then the shoes standing on it, then the legs, then the trees, and the man last of all. What holds a thing up must exist before the thing. This happens once, to open the film, and then it stops.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: He rides a bicycle. He tests where his limit is, again and again. He gets tired, and he meets the wall.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: He closes his eyes.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: From that moment the film changes its rules and never changes them back. Before, things came to him. Now nothing arrives and we move instead. Every change of place is a passage through a surface, and there is not one cut left in the film. We fly into his head as his eyes shut, through white, and a vortex takes him upward, out of the world.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: He arrives at a door already giving off light, and he is drawn through it rather than walking in. We pull back and the house assembles around us, and by the time we can see the whole building the door is shut. It is a house made of his own body.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: We fly along its corridors. The doors do not have names on them. They have shapes pressed into the clay: a muscle, a pair of lungs, a heart. He looks in each room, and there is nothing in it for him.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: Then a door with a key on it. And he goes in.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: Inside, a small brain in a chair at a wall of dials. And he has been waiting.

radio_drama.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama.text: Ah. There you are. I was expecting you.

radio_drama.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama.text: Before we start. Lift your right arm for me.

radio_drama.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama.text: I'm trying.

radio_drama.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama.text: I know.

radio_drama.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama.text: I can't. Why can't I move it?

radio_drama.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama.text: Try now.

radio_drama.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama.text: That was you. It was never my arm at all.

radio_drama.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama.text: It is always your arm. The permission is mine.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: Then the two of them put it on the boards. Neither board arrives finished. Manan writes what he was taught, in white chalk, line by line: the old theory. Coach Brain answers on the whiteboard in black marker. The same layout, the same three lines, the same gauge, and every single value reversed.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: They reach a conclusion together. Then the vortex takes him back down, and the key falls with him.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: Coach Brain lets it go, and it falls through an empty frame. It turns and it grows as it comes, and behind it the whole film replays in reverse, so faint it is almost not there: the boards, the room, the house, and the avenue as it lands. The memories are streaked in the direction of the fall because they are passing at speed, but you can still make out what each one is if you look. The key stays sharp, because the camera is falling with it, and that difference is what makes the fall feel fast.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: On the way down it crosses from a pencil drawing to a photograph, and no single frame is the moment it becomes real.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: Manan catches it at the bottom.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: Their two hands are never in the same frame, because an entire descent lies between them. That is deliberate, and it is better than a cut. A cut is a decision the audience can feel. A fall is one they take with the object.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: Credits, flying card to card through cloud. Then a dedication.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Dječak trči. Nije utrka, nije natjecanje, samo dječak na cesti. A svijet kroz koji trči ne pojavljuje se onako kako se crteži obično pojavljuju. On izranja. Kao novčić ispod papira preko kojeg se olovkom trlja, stvari izlaze iz praznog lista jedna po jedna, i uvijek istim redom. Prvo cesta, pa cipele koje na njoj stoje, pa noge, pa drveće, i tek na kraju čovjek. Ono što nešto drži mora postojati prije te stvari. To se dogodi jednom, da otvori film, i onda prestane.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Vozi bicikl. Ispituje gdje mu je granica, opet i opet. Umara se, i nailazi na zid.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Zatvara oči.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Od tog trenutka film mijenja svoja pravila i više ih ne vraća. Prije su stvari dolazile k njemu. Sada ništa ne dolazi, nego se mi krećemo. Svaka promjena mjesta je prolazak kroz površinu, i u filmu više nema nijednog reza. Ulijećemo mu u glavu dok se oči zatvaraju, kroz bijelo, i vrtlog ga podiže prema gore, izvan svijeta.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Stiže pred vrata koja već svijetle, i biva uvučen kroz njih umjesto da ušeta. Odmičemo se, i kuća se sklapa oko nas, a dok vidimo cijelu zgradu vrata su već zatvorena. To je kuća sagrađena od njegova vlastitog tijela.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Letimo njezinim hodnicima. Vrata nemaju imena na sebi. Imaju oblike utisnute u glinu: mišić, pluća, srce. Zaviruje u svaku sobu, i ni u jednoj nema ničega za njega.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Onda vrata s ključem na sebi. I ulazi.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Unutra, mali mozak u stolici pred zidom punim brojčanika. I on ga je čekao.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_hr.text: Ah. Tu si. Očekivao sam te.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_hr.text: Prije nego počnemo. Podigni mi desnu ruku.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_hr.text: Pokušavam.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_hr.text: Znam.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_hr.text: Ne mogu. Zašto je ne mogu pomaknuti?

radio_drama_hr.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_hr.text: Probaj sada.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_hr.text: To si bio ti. Nikada to nije ni bila moja ruka.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_hr.text: Ruka je uvijek tvoja. Dopuštenje je moje.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Onda njih dvojica to iznose na ploče. Nijedna ploča ne dolazi gotova. Manan bijelom kredom piše ono što su ga učili, redak po redak. Stara teorija.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_hr.text: Tisuću devetsto dvadeset treća. Hill stavlja trkače na traku i mjeri sve što rade. Njegov odgovor je jednostavan. Umor je u mišiću.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_hr.text: Trčiš. Mišić troši svoj kisik. Gorivo se potroši. I kad spremnik pokaže prazno, tijelo stane.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Coach Brain odgovara na bijeloj ploči crnim markerom. Isti raspored, ista tri retka, isti mjerač, i svaka vrijednost obrnuta.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_hr.text: Puls, dah, temperatura, voda, udaljenost. Čitam sve to, cijelo vrijeme. I postavljam jedno pitanje: možemo li nastaviti sigurno?

radio_drama_hr.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_hr.text: Kad odgovor počne izgledati kao ne, usporim te. Dakle ne. Umor je u mozgu, a ne u tvojim nogama. Ovdje gore. I odlučuje mnogo prije nego što je išta stvarno u opasnosti.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_hr.text: Kad te ja zaustavim, gorivo je još uvijek tu.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_hr.text: Znači zid...

radio_drama_hr.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_hr.text: Je broj koji sam ja odabrao. Pažljivo. Da te održim na životu.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_hr.text: Onda to može biti i drugi broj.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Dolaze do zaključka zajedno. Onda ga vrtlog nosi natrag dolje, i ključ pada s njim.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Coach Brain ga pušta, i on pada kroz prazan kadar. Okreće se i raste dok dolazi, a iza njega se cijeli film vrti unatrag, tako blijedo da ga gotovo nema. Ploče, soba, kuća, i drvored dok slijeće. Sjećanja su razvučena u smjeru pada jer prolaze brzinom, ali još uvijek možeš razabrati što je svako od njih ako pogledaš. Ključ ostaje oštar, jer kamera pada s njim, i ta razlika je ono što čini da pad djeluje brzo.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Na putu prema dolje prelazi iz crteža olovkom u fotografiju, i nijedan pojedini kadar nije trenutak u kojem postaje stvaran.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Manan ga hvata na dnu.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Njihove dvije ruke nikada nisu u istom kadru, jer između njih leži cijeli pad. To je namjerno, i bolje je od reza. Rez je odluka koju publika osjeti. Pad je odluka koju uzmu zajedno s predmetom.

radio_drama_hr.text: Odjavna špica, od kartice do kartice, kroz oblake.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Posvećeno Gospodinu Ganeshi. Uklonitelju prepreka.

Ploče, soba, kuća, i drvored dok slijeće. Sjećanja su razvučena u smjeru pada jer prolaze brzinom, ali još uvijek možeš razabrati što je svako od njih ako pogledaš. Ključ ostaje oštar, jer kamera pada s njim, i ta razlika je ono što čini da pad djeluje brzo.

radio_drama_v3.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v3.text: Na putu prema dolje prelazi iz crteža olovkom u fotografiju, i nijedan pojedini kadar nije trenutak u kojem postaje stvaran.

radio_drama_v3.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v3.text: Manan ga hvata na dnu.

radio_drama_v3.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v3.text: Odjavna špica, od kartice do kartice, kroz oblake.

radio_drama_v3.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v3.text: Posvećeno Gospodinu Ganeshi. Uklonitelju prepreka.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Maratonac trči. Duga cesta, ravnomjeran korak, čovjek koji ovo radi cijeli život.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: A svijet kroz koji trči ne pojavljuje se onako kako se crteži obično pojavljuju. On izranja. Kao novčić ispod papira preko kojeg se olovkom trlja, stvari izlaze iz praznog lista jedna po jedna, i uvijek istim redom. Priroda prije nego itko u njoj stoji. Prvo cesta, jer bez ceste nema ni drveća uz nju. Onda drveće. Onda cipele koje stoje na cesti, pa noge, i tek na kraju čovjek.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: I onda ga gledamo kako se raspada.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Korak mu se lomi. Ramena padaju. Glava mu visi. Noge više ne slušaju kako treba, i svaki sljedeći korak izgleda kao da bi mogao biti zadnji. Posrće. Pada. Diže se, i trči dalje, ali to više nije trčanje, to je čovjek koji se odbija zaustaviti.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Prazan je. Nema više ništa u njemu. Svatko tko ovo gleda zna kako to izgleda kad je gotovo.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: A onda, na kraju ceste, nešto se pojavi.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Traka. Natpis preko ceste. Cilj.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: I on ga vidi.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: A onda se dogodi ono što je srce ovog filma. Trenutak u kojem se nešto otpusti.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Kamera ulazi u njega. Koža postaje prozirna, kao da je papir kroz koji se vidi, i pod njom se ukaže cijela građa: mišići, vlakna, tetive, sve isprepleteno i sve umorno. Mrtvo. Sivo.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: I onda se upali.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Prvo jedan mišić u listu, kao žica koja je dobila struju. Pa drugi, iznad njega. Pa cijelo bedro. Svjetlo putuje kroz njegovo tijelo, od stopala prema gore, mišić po mišić, kao da negdje netko jedan po jedan pušta prekidače. Ono što je sekundu prije bilo sivo, sada gori.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Nije to novo gorivo. Nije mu nitko ništa dao. To je bilo tu cijelo vrijeme, samo zatvoreno, i netko je upravo odlučio otvoriti.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Koža se vraća. Svjetlo ostaje ispod nje.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: I čovjek koji prije pet sekundi nije imao ništa, sada sprinta. Glava gore, ramena natrag, korak kratak i brz. Sprinta prema traci brže nego što je trčao cijelu utrku.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Odakle mu to? Spremnik je bio prazan. Vidjeli smo da je bio prazan.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: I tu se kadar zaledi. Trkač ostane zaustavljen usred koraka, ruka u zraku, jedna noga još ne dodiruje tlo.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: A u taj zaleđeni kadar ušeta dječak.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Manan. S povećalom u ruci, kao Sherlock Holmes koji je upravo ušao u mjesto zločina. Obilazi trkača. Sagne se. Pogleda mu noge kroz povećalo, pa lice, pa traku na kraju ceste. Nešto se ovdje ne slaže i on to zna.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Ako je gorivo bilo potrošeno, odakle sprint? A ako sprint postoji, onda gorivo nije bilo potrošeno. Netko je lagao.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Ovdje film dobiva svoju temu. Nije riječ o čovjeku koji trči, nego o dječaku koji želi znati zašto čovjek stane, i zašto odjednom prestane stajati.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Radoznalost postaje pokus. Izvodi bicikl na ulicu i sam gura granicu, jer pitanje na kojem možeš voziti bolje je od pitanja koje možeš samo čitati.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Onda u sobi, na trenažeru, s vlastitom ranijom vožnjom koja se vrti na laptopu pred njim. Utrkuje se sam sa sobom. Nema protivnika, nema sata, nitko ne gleda. Jedino što pokušava pobijediti jest ono što je njegovo vlastito tijelo napravilo prije sat vremena. Gura dok se ne sruši.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Zatvara oči.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Od tog trenutka film mijenja svoja pravila i više ih ne vraća. Prije su stvari dolazile k njemu. Sada ništa ne dolazi, nego se mi krećemo. Svaka promjena mjesta je prolazak kroz površinu, i u filmu više nema nijednog reza. Ulijećemo mu u glavu dok se oči zatvaraju, kroz bijelo, i vrtlog ga podiže prema gore, izvan svijeta.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Stiže pred vrata koja već svijetle, i biva uvučen kroz njih umjesto da ušeta. Odmičemo se, i kuća se sklapa oko nas, a dok vidimo cijelu zgradu vrata su već zatvorena. To je kuća sagrađena od njegova vlastitog tijela.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Letimo njezinim hodnicima. Vrata nemaju imena na sebi. Imaju oblike utisnute u glinu: mišić, pluća, srce. Zaviruje u svaku sobu, i ni u jednoj nema ničega za njega.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Onda vrata s ključem na sebi. I ulazi.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Unutra, mali mozak u stolici pred zidom punim brojčanika. I on ga je čekao.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Coach Brain kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_v6.text: Ah. Tu si. Očekivao sam te.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Coach Brain kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_v6.text: Prije nego počnemo. Podigni mi desnu ruku.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Manan kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_v6.text: Pokušavam.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Coach Brain kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_v6.text: Znam.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Manan kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_v6.text: Ne mogu. Zašto je ne mogu pomaknuti?

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Coach Brain kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_v6.text: Probaj sada.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Manan kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_v6.text: To si bio ti. Nikada to nije ni bila moja ruka.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Coach Brain kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_v6.text: Ruka je uvijek tvoja. Dopuštenje je moje.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Onda njih dvojica to iznose na ploče. Nijedna ploča ne dolazi gotova. Manan bijelom kredom piše ono što su ga učili, redak po redak. Stara teorija.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Manan kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_v6.text: Tisuću devetsto dvadeset treća. Hill stavlja trkače na traku i mjeri sve što rade. Njegov odgovor je jednostavan. Umor je u mišiću.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Manan kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_v6.text: Trčiš. Mišić troši svoj kisik. Gorivo se potroši. I kad spremnik pokaže prazno, tijelo stane.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Coach Brain odgovara na bijeloj ploči crnim markerom. Isti raspored, ista tri retka, isti mjerač, i svaka vrijednost obrnuta.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Coach Brain kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_v6.text: Puls, dah, temperatura, voda, udaljenost. Čitam sve to, cijelo vrijeme. I postavljam jedno pitanje: možemo li nastaviti sigurno?

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Coach Brain kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_v6.text: Kad odgovor počne izgledati kao ne, usporim te. Dakle ne. Umor je u mozgu, a ne u tvojim nogama. Ovdje gore. I odlučuje mnogo prije nego što je išta stvarno u opasnosti.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Coach Brain kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_v6.text: Kad te ja zaustavim, gorivo je još uvijek tu.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Manan kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_v6.text: Znači zid...

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Coach Brain kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: COACH BRAIN
radio_drama_v6.text: Je broj koji sam ja odabrao. Pažljivo. Da te održim na životu.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Manan kaže.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_v6.text: Onda to može biti i drugi broj.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Dolaze do zaključka zajedno. Onda ga vrtlog nosi natrag dolje, i ključ pada s njim.

Ključ ostaje oštar, jer kamera pada s njim, i ta razlika je ono što čini da pad djeluje brzo.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Na putu prema dolje prelazi iz crteža olovkom u fotografiju, i nijedan pojedini kadar nije trenutak u kojem postaje stvaran.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Manan ga hvata na dnu.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Odjavna špica, od kartice do kartice, kroz oblake.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: I ako se sada odmakneš i pogledaš cijeli film odjednom, vidiš da je to putovanje. Prvo trči. Onda vozi. Onda leti. Uspinje se, sve više i više. A onda pada.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: To je stari oblik, stariji od filma. Junak se uzdiže, junak umire, i junak se vraća s nečim što prije nije imao. Manan se vraća s ključem. I sa spoznajom da zid nije zid, nego postavka. Broj koji je netko odabrao, i koji se može promijeniti.

radio_drama_v6.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v6.text: Posvećeno Gospodinu Ganeshi. Uklonitelju prepreka.
